key_insight: Vine Codes are low-overhead qLDPC codes that keep superconducting hardware compatibility by using nearest-neighbour gates on a planar square grid with open boundaries and routing qubits.
engineering_relevance: They offer a practical path to reduce qubit count versus the surface code while remaining implementable with native iSWAP and CZ operations on near-term superconducting devices.
method: Searches for candidate vine codes on planar square grids with routing qubits.
Verifies circuit distances and compares qubit overhead against the surface code.
Introduces Flip-Vine Codes with transversal Clifford gates and generalized open-boundary constructions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports candidate codes such as [[121,4,6]], [[221,6,7]], and [[234,9,6]], with up to ~28% fewer data+measure qubits at circuit distance 7 and ~18% fewer total qubits at distance 10, plus improved circuit-level performance at noise rate 10^-3.
watch_item: Performance and qubit savings depend on routing-qubit layout, circuit-distance verification, and realistic hardware noise assumptions, so implementation complexity may offset some gains.
paper_title: Vine Codes: Low-Overhead Quantum LDPC Codes on a Planar Square Grid
